review.notes: No Yugipedia Card Errata page (packet `errata_page.missing: true`); literal texts copied from the packet and byte-identical between the GOAT entry and `modern_text`, so the whole difference is ruling-layer. Verified against goat/c504700109.lua vs official/c65878864.lua; upstream's own annotation on the variant, 'It targets up to 2 monsters', matches the script. Two distinct in-play consequences follow and both are recorded in the summary: activation with a single targetable monster on the field, and partial resolution when one of two targets is no longer relatable. Considered `engine`: nothing in data/rule-profiles/tcg-goat.json governs per-card target-count requirements, so this is correctly a card-level ruling record and not a rule-profile matter. Chronology unresolved - no dated source for the era target-count semantics is available in the packet, and this card is absent from EdisonFormat.com's functional-errata list (the 'Nobleman' entries there are Nobleman of Crossout / Nobleman of Extermination, different cards, and are not evidence for this one).

event.historical_text: FLIP: Destroy 2 monsters on the field.
event.modern_text: FLIP: Destroy 2 monsters on the field.
event.summary: Era target-count semantics, not a text erratum: the GOAT script targets UP TO 2 monsters - it counts targetable monsters, sets `ct=math.min(ct,2)` and calls `Duel.SelectTarget(tp,aux.TRUE,tp,LOCATION_MZONE,LOCATION_MZONE,ct,2,nil)`, so the Flip effect still works when only one monster can be targeted and destroys that one, and at resolution it destroys whatever targets remain (`if #sg<1 then return end`). The modern script requires two targetable monsters to exist (`Duel.IsExistingTarget(aux.TRUE,...,2,nil)`), selects exactly 2, and destroys nothing at all unless both targets are still related to the effect (`if #sg~=2 then return end`). Targeting itself is unchanged - `EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET` and the `chkc` Monster-Zone check are present in both - and the cdb text is identical, so this is a ruling-layer difference in how many targets the effect demands.
